title: super-board flow: OMP + Python

kinds.public: skill or command you run directly
kinds.lane: board lane: started by /super-board run, also runnable standalone
kinds.external: skill from another pack (origin says where)
kinds.script: shell, python or node script a skill runs
kinds.hook: host extension that fires on its own
kinds.board: state: GitHub Project, config, ledgers, worktrees

notes: Fork ratopythonista/super-board @ v3.4.0-omp.1: upstream 3.4.0 plus the OMP host and lane backend.
Source paths are repo-root-relative; nodes from another pack (mattpocock/skills, ratopythonista/skills) show their path as text.
Generated by `visual.py skillmap` on the installed .agents/skills, then enriched with the OMP and Python delta.

nodes.label: /git-sync
nodes.what: Commits one logical change at a time, pulls, resolves conflicts hunk by hunk and pushes without force.
nodes.when: You run `/git-sync` or say "sync".
nodes.how: Never stages secrets, never force pushes, never skips a hook.

nodes.label: /pr-security-review
nodes.what: Reviews one PR's diff against its base for exploitable, high-confidence vulnerabilities.
nodes.when: Before merging anything that touches auth, input handling or secrets.
nodes.how: Reports only findings it can trace to a line of the diff.

nodes.label: pytest-fasthtml
nodes.what: Test mechanics for Python/FastHTML: where a test belongs (unit, integration, e2e), fixtures, async handlers, HTMX requests, Playwright and the `uv`/`ruff` commands.
nodes.when: A card's `Skills:` line names it, or any pytest + FastHTML work starts.
nodes.how: Published from `ratopythonista/skills`; installed with `npx skills add ratopythonista/skills/tree/main/skills/pytest-fasthtml` and pinned in `skills-lock.json`.
nodes.author: ratopythonista

nodes.label: /super-board
nodes.what: Drives one GitHub Project from Backlog to Done: five verbs, seven columns, labels `qa` · `bug` · `feature` routing each card.
nodes.when: You type `/super-board <verb>`, or say "drain my project".
nodes.how: Under OMP a plain `run` counts as `--omp`: every lane is a headless `omp -p`, because the host has no Workflow tool.

nodes.label: /super-board onboard
nodes.what: one-time setup wizard; writes .claude/super-board/configs/<slug>.json
nodes.when: User runs `/super-board onboard`

nodes.label: /super-board lint
nodes.what: walks active-pipeline issues, flags vague ACs, runs pre-flight readiness
nodes.when: User runs `/super-board lint`

nodes.label: /super-board status
nodes.what: snapshot of active config, column counts, in-flight workers
nodes.when: User runs `/super-board status`

nodes.label: /super-board run
nodes.what: Plans a wave, dispatches Build → QA → Review and applies the merge gate, one card at a time per column.
nodes.when: `/super-board run [--low|--high] [--omp] [slug]`.
nodes.how: `--omp` resolves model roles from `omp.modelRoles`; Review always `@review`, the truth-check `@task`.

nodes.label: /super-board stop
nodes.what: graceful shutdown: posts "stopped mid-flight" comments on every in-flight issue + PR, releases assignee mutexes, kills workers + dispatcher. Next super-board run resumes.
nodes.when: User runs `/super-board stop`

nodes.label: super-build
nodes.what: Takes a `Ready` card into its own worktree, writes the change, runs the project's verify commands and opens a PR.
nodes.when: The wave claims the card.
nodes.how: `omp -p --mode json --model @hard` inside `<run>/wt/<card>`; the prompt is the skill, the evidence is the PR plus `lanes.jsonl`.

nodes.label: /super-collect
nodes.what: Finds problems in one project, verifies each, writes one findings doc and hands it to `/to-tickets`.
nodes.when: Bugs, gaps or a repo you want audited.
nodes.how: Every finding is verified before it becomes a ticket, so the board never receives a guess.

nodes.label: super-qa
nodes.what: Checks the diff against the card's acceptance criteria, runs browser-level proof, files findings as one issue and moves the card to Review or back to Building.
nodes.when: Build opened a PR.
nodes.how: Playwright runs here, not in `verify_commands`, so the fast checks stay fast.

nodes.label: super-review
nodes.what: Reviews Standards × Spec in a fresh context and returns `approved`, `bounced` or `failed` as schema-checked JSON.
nodes.when: QA is green.
nodes.how: Always `@review`; a bounce keeps the PR and sends the card back to Building with the findings.

nodes.label: /ui-refine-loop
nodes.what: Unattended Impeccable check → fix loop on one page or component.
nodes.when: Use when the user says "ui-refine-loop", "/ui-refine-loop", "refine loop", "iterate on this page", "polish this page with impeccable", or "keep polishing".
nodes.how: Impeccable's `critique` and `audit` find problems once, and each fix command (`distill`, `layout`, `polish`, and the rest) fixes one kind once. This skill chains them into a short unattended loop. Each round, **fresh checkers** find and rank the problems, then a **fresh fixer** picks the right Impeccable commands and lands one green commit. A short ledger is the only thing carried between rounds,

nodes.label: /visual
nodes.what: Turns the work into one self-contained HTML page: a recap, a plan, a folder or architecture map, or an interactive drill-down map.
nodes.when: You run `/visual`, or ask to visualise a branch, a plan or a system.
nodes.how: `visual.py skillmap` writes the skeleton from `SKILL.md`; `render --map` bakes a crossing-free layout, links sources and runs the checks.

nodes.label: /visual recap
nodes.what: Recaps a branch or PR as one HTML page: what changed, why, and the diff that proves it.
nodes.when: `/visual recap [base]`.
nodes.how: `visual.py facts` reads git, then `render` bakes the layout and runs the checks.

nodes.label: /visual plan
nodes.what: Turns a plan file into a page: steps, the mechanism as a diagram, and the files each step touches.
nodes.when: `/visual plan <file>`.
nodes.how: Read-only: nothing in the repo changes while the plan is visualised.

nodes.label: /visual map
nodes.what: Maps a folder, an endpoint set or an architecture as a drill-down page.
nodes.when: `/visual map <path|map.json>`.
nodes.how: This page is that mode: `skillmap` writes the skeleton, `render --map` scores a crossing-free layout.

nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.label: super-board-gh-guard.sh
nodes.what: Worker-side `gh` rate-limit etiquette: lanes share one token bucket so parallel workers cannot drain the 5000/hr GraphQL quota.
nodes.when: Sourced by Build, QA and Review before a burst of `gh` calls.
nodes.how: It is the worker-side half of `gh_rate_guard`, which only protects the dispatcher's own ticks.

nodes.label: super-build-dispatch.sh

nodes.when: The Claude backend runs Build.
nodes.how: The OMP backend uses `super-board-omp-lane.sh` instead: same contract, different host call.

nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.author: mattpocock

nodes.what: Files a deepening opportunity found in review as a ticket instead of holding a green PR.

nodes.label: shoot.mjs

nodes.label: wizard
nodes.what: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform.
nodes.when: Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

nodes.label: Needs triage
nodes.what: Every request lands as a GitHub issue labelled `needs-triage`; nothing reaches the board before it has one.
nodes.when: Start of a work item.
nodes.how: Fuzzy premise → `grill-with-docs` or `wayfinder`. Bug or gap found in the repo → `super-collect`.

nodes.label: Contract gate
nodes.what: A human approves observable acceptance criteria, invariants and non-scope before a card becomes `ready-for-agent`. It replaces reading every diff.
nodes.when: Before any lane runs.
nodes.how: Approval is the authorisation; `always_human` still covers security, auth, migrations and secrets.

nodes.label: classifier
nodes.what: A cheap router grades each card easy, medium or hard before the wave picks its model.
nodes.when: Once per card, at the head of the wave.
nodes.how: Under `--omp` the grade maps to `@medium`/`@hard`; `--low` and `--high` shift the ladder.

nodes.label: wave
nodes.what: Claims up to four `Ready` cards, runs them in parallel and serializes the Review lane.
nodes.when: A card is `Ready` and unblocked.
nodes.how: A lane that returns no usable result and leaves the card in place is retried once; a lane that moved the card or returned a valid `failed` is never retried.

nodes.label: Card
nodes.what: One issue on the GitHub Project with observable acceptance criteria and declared dependencies; an optional `Skills:` line names the skills its lane must read.
nodes.when: The wave claims it.
nodes.how: It is the unit of state: `Ready` → `Building` → `QA` → `Review` → `Done`.

nodes.label: Worktree
nodes.what: One checkout per card, cut from the base branch, so lanes never touch the main tree.
nodes.when: When the card is claimed.
nodes.how: Lanes do not push; the merge gate merges the branch after the checks pass.

nodes.label: Merge gate
nodes.what: Merges only when the base plus your non-empty `verify_commands` pass, pinned to the reviewed commit; applies `merge_policy` and the 400-product-line auto-merge cap.
nodes.when: Review approved.
nodes.how: `always_human` (security, auth, migrations, secrets) and the size cap hand the decision back to a person.

nodes.label: Functional acceptance
nodes.what: A human validates behaviour at the end of a milestone with QA evidence, never by reading every diff.
nodes.when: Milestone closes.
nodes.how: A broken premise sends the work back to grilling, not to a patch.

nodes.label: CONTEXT · ADR
nodes.what: Docs are written when they crystallise: a glossary term the moment it is resolved, an ADR only when the decision is hard to reverse, surprising and a real trade-off.
nodes.when: A term or a decision settles.
nodes.how: Batching is the failure mode: an unresolved term silently drifts.

nodes.label: super-board-host.sh
nodes.what: Prints one host value; first match wins: `SUPER_BOARD_HOST`, then OMP's signs (`OMPCODE`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, `OMP_PROFILE`), Codex, OpenCode, `CLAUDECODE`, the config `host`, else exit 65.
nodes.when: Every `/super-board` command and every lane.
nodes.how: OMP exports `CLAUDECODE=1` too, so its own signs are checked first; a live env sign beats the saved config. It never guesses Claude.

nodes.label: super-board-omp-lane.sh
nodes.what: Runs one lane as a headless OMP call and validates the lane schema against the result JSON.
nodes.when: The wave dispatches a lane, or you diagnose one card.
nodes.how: `omp -p --mode json --tools read,bash,edit,write,grep,glob,web_search[,task] --config <run>/roles.yml --model @<role> --max-time/--max-cost --no-extensions -e .omp/extensions/super-board-guards.ts`; falls back to the last NDJSON assistant message. Exit 3 → `halted`/`cost-cap`, a deadline → `halted`/`time-cap`.

nodes.label: super-board-omp-wave.sh
nodes.what: Drains the board four cards at a time, serializes Review, retries once a lane that produced nothing, and keeps the wave marker.
nodes.when: `bash .claude/bin/super-board-omp-wave.sh --config <cfg> --cards <json> --omp`.
nodes.how: Writes `wave-result.json` and `lanes.jsonl` beside `--output`, and `omp-wave.pid`; `super-board-stop.sh` sweeps the `omp -p` orphans.

nodes.label: super-board-guards.ts
nodes.what: OMP extension that stops a lane from writing outside its worktree and blocks pushes that the board must own.
nodes.when: Loaded by every OMP lane through `-e .omp/extensions/super-board-guards.ts`.
nodes.how: It is the OMP answer to Claude's hook settings: same guards, enforced by the host extension instead of `.claude/settings.json`.

nodes.label: roles.yml
nodes.what: Per-run model roles resolved from `omp.modelRoles`, with `retry.fallbackChains` nested under `retry`.
nodes.when: Written at the head of a run.
nodes.how: `run --omp` → router `@classify`, easy card `@medium`, medium and hard `@hard`; `--low`/`--high` shift the ladder. Review always `@review`, truth-check `@task`.

nodes.label: omp.limits
nodes.what: Flat caps per lane: classify $0.05/3m, build $0.50/30m, qa $0.30/20m, review $0.75/30m.
nodes.when: Every lane.
nodes.how: They replace Claude's usage guard: a cap ends the lane as `halted` and leaves the card, claim, worktree and PR in place.

nodes.label: lanes.jsonl
nodes.what: One record per lane: `{ts, card, lane, role, provider, model, thinking, cost, status}`, plus the `@classify` grade with `complexity`.
nodes.when: Every wave and every single lane, beside `--output`.
nodes.how: `jq -r '[.card,.lane,.role,.provider,.model,.thinking,.cost] | @tsv' lanes.jsonl` is the model table of the run, taken from the run itself — no probe.

nodes.label: wave-result.json
nodes.what: Per-card outcome: `finalStatus`, `lastLane`, `column`, `detail`, `prUrl`, `lanesRun`.
nodes.when: The wave ends.
nodes.how: A lane that died after moving the card is reported with the card's real column, read once from the board.

nodes.label: board config
nodes.what: `.claude/super-board/configs/<slug>.json`: project, columns, labels, `host`, the `omp.*` block, `merge_policy`, `verify_commands` and `paths.pre_flight_md`.
nodes.when: `/super-board onboard` writes it; `setup.py check` validates it.
nodes.how: `worker_backend` is inherited from the Claude-era config and is not used by the OMP backend: `--omp` is what selects the lanes.

nodes.label: verify_commands
nodes.what: The project's own checks, non-empty: `uv sync --frozen`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest -q`.
nodes.when: Build, and again at the merge gate.
nodes.how: A missing list halts setup instead of merging on faith; the gate re-runs them pinned to the reviewed commit.

nodes.label: Playwright e2e
nodes.what: Browser-level proof of the user flow, kept out of `verify_commands` because it is slow.
nodes.when: The QA lane.
nodes.how: Chromium is installed once per machine (`npx playwright install chromium`, or the Python equivalent).

nodes.label: pre-flight
nodes.what: Repo pre-flight the board reads before dispatching: `docs/super-board/pre-flight-python.md` in the project.
nodes.when: Before the first wave of a project.
nodes.how: It names the stack, the commands and the paths the lanes must not touch.

nodes.label: GitHub Project
nodes.what: The board itself: Backlog · Ready · Building · QA · Review · Blocked · Done, with native issue dependencies as the blocking edges.
nodes.when: Always.
nodes.how: `qa` skips Building; a dropped card is closed as not planned and lands in Done.

nodes.label: Human decision
nodes.what: Where the run stops and hands back: contract refused, size cap, or an `always_human` trigger.
nodes.when: Policy says a person must decide.
nodes.how: Nothing merges on the strength of an agent's own check.

nodes.label: super-board-merge-policy.py
nodes.what: Reads `human_approves_merge`, `merge_policy.default` and the always-human list to decide auto or human.
nodes.when: The merge gate reached a green verified commit.
nodes.how: `size_cap` counts product lines, not the diff of generated files.

nodes.label: get.sh
nodes.what: One-line installer: fetches the `codeload` tarball for a ref (default: latest release) and runs `install.sh`.
nodes.when: You install the pack into a project.
nodes.how: `SUPER_BOARD_REPO` picks the owner/repo, `--ref` the tag or branch, `--hosts` the host folders.

nodes.label: install.sh
nodes.what: Copies `skills/`, `scripts/`, `workflows/` and `hooks/` into `.agents/`, links every host folder and merges the hook settings once.
nodes.when: `get.sh`, or a checkout with `./install.sh`.
nodes.how: `.agents/` is canonical; `.claude/` is always linked, `.omp/` when asked or detected. `--protect-main` adds the push guard.

nodes.label: super-board-setup.py
nodes.what: Verifies the installed surfaces and the board config; `fix` adds a missing `host`.
nodes.when: `/super-board onboard` checks, or right after installing.
nodes.how: `check --root <dir> --pack <pack> --host omp` lists `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills` and `.omp/skills`.

nodes.label: v3.4.0-omp.1
nodes.what: This fork's release tag: upstream 3.4.0 plus the OMP host and lane backend.
nodes.when: You install from the fork.
nodes.how: `VERSION` stays `3.4.0`; the tag names the fork's provenance, so it cannot collide with the upstream's own 3.4.0.

views.title: Development flow · OMP + Python
views.caption: Ideas enter at wayfinder or grill-with-docs, bugs at super-collect; both meet at /to-spec and /to-tickets, and a human approves the contract before the board runs. The delta over the upstream pack is the OMP lane and the Python verify stack; everything green goes through the merge gate.

views.title: Contrato · spec before code
views.caption: One door per kind of work. Nothing reaches the board while a premise is a guess: the card is executable only after a human approves AC, invariants and non-scope.

views.title: Fábrica · card → wave → Build → QA → Review
views.caption: Four cards per wave. Review always runs in a fresh context; a bounce returns the card to Building with the findings and keeps the PR.

views.title: Lane OMP · omp -p, roles and caps
views.caption: The pack's Claude backend uses a Workflow tool and hooks; OMP has neither. The delta is one backend script, model roles resolved from the config, flat cost/time caps per lane, and a host extension instead of hook settings.

views.title: Lane Python · uv, ruff, pytest
views.caption: The same vertical slice proved in TS/React was repeated in Python/FastHTML: `uv sync --frozen`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest -q` in verify_commands, and Playwright only in QA.

views.title: Merge gate · verify, cap and policy
views.caption: A green run is not an authorisation. The gate re-runs the project's checks on the reviewed commit, counts product lines, and hands the decision back when policy says a person owns it.

views.title: Aceite · milestone, evidence, docs
views.caption: Behaviour is accepted by a human at the end of a milestone with QA evidence. Documentation is written when a term or a decision settles, not at the end.

views.title: Install · from the fork
views.caption: `get.sh` fetches the tag, `install.sh` lays down `.agents/` and links the hosts, `super-board-setup.py check --host omp` proves it, `onboard` writes the config.

views.title: Referência · o resto do pack
views.caption: The pack's other skills, scripts and state, captured by the generator and kept reachable: they run outside the flow (or on their own schedule).
